name: ref_sTRlKTYrx_E
summary: An informative, essay-style tutorial combining direct-to-camera presentation with timeline screen recordings and demonstrative B-roll. It relies on retro pixel-font title cards, audio-driven J-cuts, and visual guidelines to clearly explain video editing concepts.

captions.notes: Captions appear as retro pixel-text cards enclosed in solid black rectangular blocks for key quotes or chapter titles rather than full continuous transcription.

headline.notes: Monospaced chapter title cards framed inside stark black boxes against colored vignette or blurred backdrops.

callouts.notes: Pixelated pointer cursors, crosshair eyeline guides, and red strike-through X icons illustrate editing dos and don'ts.

transitions.notes: Heavy emphasis on smooth J-cuts with audio leading the visual edit by 2-3 frames, supplemented by clean hard cuts and match cuts.

rules: Lead incoming visuals with dialog audio by 2 to 4 frames (J-cut)
Use solid black rectangular cards with pixel-art font for section headers
Maintain strict eyeline consistency across jump cuts using frame guides
Support editing arguments with actual NLE timeline screengrabs
Cut aggressively to B-roll to prevent monologue fatigue
Keep camera framing natural without hyperactive digital zoom punches
Use pixelated cursor overlays and crosshairs to highlight technical elements
Keep camera framing exclusively on the speaker.
Cut strictly on natural sentence or thought completions.
Alternate framings between medium-wide and tight punch-in.
Let ambient and vocal pauses breathe without hard audio truncation.
Maintain subtle, emotional background music under dialogue.
avoid: Excessive zoom-in punch cuts on every sentence
Fast trendy motion graphics and kinetic typography
Aggressive whip pans or flashy transition plugins
Leaving talking head uninterrupted for more than 10 seconds
